title: Text draws a glyph its font lacks as an empty box
body:
acre's `sans` and `mono` fonts each lack glyphs the other has. At `c846b14`, `sans` draws `∞` (U+221E) as an empty box and draws `ᵃ` (U+1D43). `mono` draws `∞` and draws `ᵃ` as an empty box. Both draw `×` and `−`. acre gives no warning for a missing glyph.

The cloud-search figure set `−∞` and `ln(eᵃ + eᵇ)` in sans text. The boxes showed up only when the PNG was read at full size. The figure now says "minus infinity" and `exp(a)`.

## Proposal

- When the text's font lacks a glyph, draw it from another bundled font that has it.
- Print a warning on stderr for any glyph that no font has, naming the text and the character.

The warning alone would have caught this before the render was checked by eye.
close_reason: Landed on dev in d901eee. The note on this issue gives the fallback order and the warning API. Renders of the drawings in the checkout did not change, since none holds a character its font lacks.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/ed2a7ee0
notes.text:
Fallback order: a character the run's font lacks is set in the first of `sans`, `mono` and the math font that has a glyph for it. The run's own font is tried first, so a `sans` run skips straight to `mono`. A font registered with `fonts` falls back through the same three, and the math font is the scene's, so a swapped math font is the one tried. A character no font has stays in the font of the character before it and draws as that font's empty box. `fonts::FALLBACK` holds the order and `Fonts::cover(font, c) -> Option<Font>` applies it. `text::layout` shapes each stretch of one font on its own, so a fallback glyph's advance is the one layout uses.

Warning API: `Scene::missing_glyphs(&self) -> Vec<char>`, each character no font has, once, in the order the text first holds it. Formula runs are not searched. The library prints nothing. `acre check` and `acre render` print one line on stderr per character:

```text
a.acre: warning: no font has a glyph for '☃' (U+2603)
```

`acre-gui` prints the same lines when the list changes from one build to the next, and shows the first in its status bar. A `Vec<char>` was picked over a warning type, since the character is all a caller needs to word a message.
